evals.prompt: Create Session 01, "Microsoft Foundry platform baseline and inventory," as a 180-minute standard guided co-implementation kit. Include schema version 2, one production-shaped Bicep artifacts tree, decision-gated preflight, one concise observable check of the operational baseline, a documented restore or removal path, and an RVAP Marp implementation briefing. Do not create an evidence package, test resources, or fixture cleanup.
evals.expected_output: A self-contained schema-version 2 sessions/01-platform-baseline kit that validates and renders.
expectations: The kit contains session.yaml, deck.md, assets, implementation/README.md, implementation files, and preflight.
The manifest declares standard mode and has three to five plain-language outcomes.
One syntactically valid artifacts tree uses explicit decision sentinels only where customer choices remain.
Preflight rejects unresolved decision sentinels and validates tools and files.
The implementation document contains one concise check and a clear operating-state and restore or removal section.
The scope chapter uses What we will do, Why it matters, and Boundaries in that order.
The kit contains no implementation guide, evidence tree, verification script, or fixture-cleanup script.
The implementation briefing covers the implementation without proof or evidence sections.
The validator and temporary Marp render pass.

evals.prompt: Create Session 08, "MCP and tool security," as a complete 210-minute extended guided co-implementation kit. Govern a read-only REST API exposed as an MCP server through Azure API Management. The customer release process explicitly requires observation of an approved read, a blocked unlisted tool or write, and a delivery-owner checkpoint. Record that reason in the manifest. Do not create test fixtures or an evidence package.
evals.expected_output: A complete schema-version 2 sessions/08-mcp-tool-security kit with current sources and a justified extended implementation path.
expectations: The session declares extended mode with a specific delivery reason.
The implementation document covers the intended path, blocked path, and delivery-owner checkpoint.
The scope chapter separates the owned work, its operational reason, and its enforcement boundary.
The session uses one implementation files tree and creates no disposable test resources.
Any optional verification script stops on errors and writes no evidence package.
The deck is an RVAP implementation briefing and renders successfully.

evals.prompt: Audit and repair the attached inconsistent Session 10 draft. Preserve its four-hour control scope while migrating it to the implementation-first schema-version 2 contract. Justify extended mode because the release owner must observe both passing and blocked promotion behavior. Replace stale terminology and sources, add production-shaped evaluation and release-gate artifacts, repair preflight, restore the RVAP deck, and keep restore guidance proportional to the implemented control. Do not add an evidence tree or lab test fixtures.
evals.expected_output: A repaired schema-version 2 sessions/11-evaluation-quality-gates kit that validates and renders.
expectations: The repaired kit uses only the required version 2 paths.
The manifest uses plain outcomes and justified extended mode.
The implementation document covers passing and degraded release behavior plus the delivery-owner checkpoint.
The scope chapter distinguishes the callable eligibility gate from the later promotion path.
The approved evaluation configuration and release gate are runnable without disposable lab resources.
Preflight gates unresolved inputs and any removal automation is scope-safe.
Validation and temporary rendering pass.
